title: Edge Telemetry Condenser SDK — unify request origin and sampling hints
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight SDK-side 'telemetry condenser' that normalizes and consolidates high-cardinality request attributes emitted from edge clients and gateways into a small set of stable, audit-friendly tracing attributes. This reduces cardinality on our traces/metrics, preserves important origin and sampling hints for downstream routing and billing, and keeps per-request overhead under the 150µs budget for hot paths.

Scope: SDK changes for Node/Python/Go SDKs, middleware for HTTP/gRPC/WebSocket transports, a small gateway handshake to exchange a compact origin token, and a server-side receiver that accepts the condensed attributes.

Key features:
- Canonical origin fields: origin_id, origin_tier, origination_region (derived and validated from header + handshake token).
- Sampling hints: condensed sampling vector (3 bits) representing priority, downstream-required, and preserve-for-audit.
- Low-cost signer verification of the handshake token using short-lived asymmetric keys.
- Fallback logic when handshake/token verification fails (mark origin as unverified and emit a metric).
- Backwards-compatibility adapter: SDK attaches condensed attributes and keeps legacy high-cardinality headers intact behind a configuration flag for 30-day rollback windows.
- Testbench: microbench harness measuring median p95 overhead across typical request sizes and KV cache hotpaths.

Acceptance criteria:
1) SDK instrumentation adds <=150µs median overhead on our Node and Go hotpath benchmarks and <=300µs on Python (interpreted) for 99th percentile.
2) Traces emitted to the collector contain the canonical origin fields in both span attributes and a top-level request envelope.
3) No increase in unique tag cardinality above the baseline (validated with a 7-day synthetic traffic run).
4) Court-approved handshake keys rotate without dropped requests during a staged key rollout.

Risks & mitigations:
- Library crypto costs: use ECDSA P-256 verification only on handshake; cache verification results for 1s per origin_id.
- Legacy clients: provide opt-out flag and automated compatibility checks in console dashboards.
- Cardinality regressions: add an ingest-side breaker to reject attributes that exceed length/cardinality heuristics and fall back to 'origin_truncated: true'.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary internal services (10% of requests) with condensed attributes enabled and legacy headers preserved. Monitor error rates and cardinality signals for 72h.
2) Expand to customer-facing edge gateways with handshake enabled for new SDK versions.
3) Full-enforce mode after 4 weeks if no regressions, with a 24h rollback switch.

Open questions for design review:
- Which exact 3-bit layout for the sampling vector provides the best balance for future signals? (proposal included in design doc).
- Key rotation timeline and operator UX for emergency revocation.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Edge+Telemetry+Condenser
- Microbench harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-microbench/tree/edge-condenser
- Spike PR (Node SDK): https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/pull/2145

Notes: this ticket is intentionally cross-cutting between SDK, gateway, and collector teams. We'll coordinate shipping the collector-side acceptance tests before final SDK enforcement.
